readerQuestion: How can Home Assistant warn me when the freezer gets too warm, repeat the warning sensibly, and let me test it without warming food?
directAnswer: Use the actual temperature sensor, an upper-only Threshold helper with a deliberate hysteresis band, and the built-in YAML Alert integration for delayed repeating reminders. Verify phone delivery with a temporary Toggle helper, then restore the real input. Missing readings and restarts can interrupt monitoring, so keep an independent appliance warning and monitor availability separately.
originalContribution: Sections 2 and 3 provide a Celsius/Fahrenheit settings worksheet and complete alert configuration. The worked-example table follows a hypothetical warming/cooling sequence through the hysteresis band and the ten-, thirty- and sixty-minute delays. Section 4 tests cancellation, repetition and acknowledgement using only a virtual switch; section 5 distinguishes sensor, notifier and restart faults.
limitations: Researched from current primary documentation and Home Assistant 2026.9.3 source; no physical freezer, sensor accuracy, battery life, RF range, installed Home Assistant instance or phone latency was tested. Notification thresholds are hypothetical settings, not safe storage limits. An isolated run of the upstream Threshold method verified nine boundary and missing-input cases, and the published YAML was parsed; these are not hardware or end-to-end installation tests. Alert timers/acknowledgement and the threshold state inside the band do not persist as a guaranteed recovery system. Phone delivery may need internet services.

claimChecks.claim: Upper-only Threshold uses strict upper+hysteresis for on and upper-hysteresis for off. Upper -14 C and hysteresis 2 C therefore starts above -12 C and clears below -16 C; lower must stay empty. Equivalent Fahrenheit settings are upper 6.8 and hysteresis 3.6.

The current Threshold implementation makes nonnumeric input unknown and does not restore its previous in-band state; the guide explicitly treats this as missing monitoring and documents the -13 C restart example. Nine isolated upstream-method cases checked equality, warming, cooling and missing data.

Alert repeat values are minutes; skip_first true plus [10,30,60] delays the first message ten minutes, the second thirty more minutes and later messages sixty minutes apart. It requires a configured notifier and configuration.yaml.

Alert stops when the watched state ceases to match on, so unknown is not a recovery verdict. Acknowledgement silences the episode; scheduled timing and acknowledgement are in-memory, not guaranteed restart catch-up.
Companion phone delivery must be configured and independently tested; notifier entries in Alert use mobile_app names without the notify prefix. No measured latency is promised.
Local Push has its own connection prerequisites. A local temperature sensor alone does not establish local phone delivery.

A Toggle helper is a virtual on/off entity, so the proposed alert-delay test need not warm food, open a freezer or switch appliance power. The test is explicitly limited to the alert and notification path.
Home Assistant OS supports editor apps; Container uses its mounted config directory. Validate configuration and restart to apply Alert YAML, preserving an existing top-level alert section.
Current Tools documentation locates Actions and YAML validation under Settings > Tools; old releases may use Developer Tools.
FDA freezer storage recommendation is 0 F / -18 C; the example warmer notification thresholds and a cleared software warning do not establish food safety.
